findings.area: Unified model vs reference: electricity factor source (defective input: grid table disagrees with its descriptor)
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/engine.py lines 664-682 (gk = grid.table) and 1059-1075; units B6-01, B6-03, B2-01, X-02, X-04, X-05, X-07, SUM-02..SUM-07
findings.claim_refuted: "evaluate(detail=True/False) reproduces every result leaf ... on deliberately defective scenarios". When grid.table differs from the parametric descriptor (the defect that X-06.matches_table exists to report), the unified model computes purchased-electricity emissions from grid.table while the reference computes them from the X-06 series built from the descriptor.
findings.evidence: Repro: scn = synth.make_scenario(23,'RC','office','S',60.0, profile_kind='LINEAR_TREND', grid_kind='LINEAR_DECLINE_TO_FLOOR', n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=4); scn.operation.grid.table[10] *= 2.0. X-06 is identical on both sides (matches_table False, by_year[11] = 0.2295867048437465). B6-01.by_year[11]: reference 27541.09395033865, unified 55082.1879006773. B6-03.value: 1572408.9404463442 vs 1599950.0343966833 (same in detail and summary mode). B2-01.value: 78834.7585503639 vs 80848.01251813363. SUM-03.value: 4500011.134141552 vs 4527552.2280918965 (0.61 %). The unified output is also inconsistent with itself: its X-06.by_year[11] is 0.2296 but its B6-01.by_year[11]/B6-04.by_year[11] is 0.4592. With CONSTANT demand profiles (same seed, profile_kind='CONSTANT') the unified B6-03 total switches to the descriptor (1555259.0777902347, equal to the reference) while its B6-01.by_year still uses the table, so the weighted sum of its own yearly series is 1582637.633967868. Which side departs: the unified model. B6-01's definition is purchased electricity times the factor of that year with depends_on X-06, and X-06's docstring builds the series from the descriptor kind. Note the definition has an ambiguity: synth/model.py does not say whether table or descriptor is authoritative for GridFactorScenario. Found by mutation 'grid.table!=descriptor(one entry)' (8/11 single-mutation runs differed). Script: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user--/49c0bd7e-a786-5ae4-9a1e-e89e7996ede3/scratchpad/verify/lens1/repro.py section F3.
findings.proposed_fix: Use one source for the factor series everywhere in engine.py (the X-06 series g_series, as the reference does), and take the closed-form path only when the table has been checked against the descriptor (matches_table True); otherwise fall back to the yearly sum. State in synth/model.py which of table/descriptor is authoritative for the grid, add 'descriptor/table mismatch' as a defect kind to the dirty generator and to verify_unified.py, and narrow the exactness claim until that passes.

findings.area: Unified model vs reference: annual profiles (defective input: profile table disagrees with CONSTANT/LINEAR_TREND descriptor)
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/engine.py lines 680-682 and 700-706 (annual(): cf.linear_weighted_sum(T, profile.base, profile.slope or 0.0)); units B6-03, B7-04, B2-01, X-02, X-04, X-05, X-07, SUM-03..SUM-07
findings.claim_refuted: Exact reproduction on defective scenarios, and the engine docstring statement that detail=False leaves totals unchanged. The unified model takes B6/B7 totals from base/slope whenever kind != TABLE; the reference reads profile.table, which synth/model.py declares authoritative ("The table is authoritative").
findings.evidence: Repro 1: scn = synth.make_scenario(24,'RC','office','S',60.0, profile_kind='CONSTANT', grid_kind='CONSTANT', n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=4); scn.water_waste.water.table[5] *= 3.0. B7-01.by_year agrees on both sides (both read the table) but B7-04.value: reference 746618.5232326112, unified 745116.5487889426; SUM-03.value: 20562520.06413958 vs 20561018.08969594. Unified detail mode returns X-07.value = 20562520.064139612 (table) next to SUM-03 = 20561018.08969594 (descriptor); unified summary mode returns X-07.value = 20561018.08969594, so the two modes of the unified model disagree with each other on the same leaf. Repro 2 (same scenario, untouched table): scn.water_waste.water.slope = 5.0 with kind still CONSTANT gives B7-04.value 745116.5487889432 (reference) vs 747092.4872335577 (unified), because the closed form uses slope even for kind CONSTANT. Repro 3: scn.operation.electricity.table[5] *= 3.0 gives B6-03.value 6784766.59802941 vs 6670420.924605405. A LINEAR_TREND table clamped at zero (table[k] = max(0, base+slope*k)) also differs and flips SUM-07.defined. Which side departs: the unified model (reference docstrings of B6-02/B6-04/B7-0x are year-by-year over the table; the model docstring makes the table authoritative). Script: repro.py section F4.
findings.proposed_fix: Before using linear_weighted_sum, verify table[k] == base + slope*k for k < Y (one pass, or a flag validated once at load) and fall back to the table sum on mismatch; ignore slope when kind is CONSTANT. Alternatively add a reference check unit that rejects descriptor/table mismatch and state that the unified model is defined only when it passes. Add this defect kind to the verification population.

findings.area: Valid scenarios: yearly repair series computed by subtraction
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/engine.py lines 1045-1055 (b3_year = repair_rate_sum*w[y] - adjustments); units B3-01 (by_year) and X-07 (by_year, cumulative), detail=True only
findings.claim_refuted: "within a relative difference of 1e-9 on valid scenarios" using the study's own criterion (compare with floor = 1e-9*|WLC|). In years where the reference is exactly 0 (every row with repairs has a renewal in that year) the unified model returns a rounding residue, sometimes negative, that exceeds the criterion.
findings.evidence: All scenarios are generator options only (dirty=False, no mutation). Repro A: synth.make_scenario(8,'RC','office','S',60.0, n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=2, service_life_choices=[0.5,1.0], explicit_event_share=0.0, change_list_share=0.0, included_stages=['B3']); WLC = 2213.8319501309584. B3-01.by_year[1]: reference 0.0, unified -5.9117155615240335e-12 (error 2.67e-6 by the study's measure); X-07.cumulative[59]: reference 0.0, unified -3.48791218129918e-10 (error 1.58e-4). Repro B, all 14 stages: synth.make_scenario(19,'RC','office','S',1.5, n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=0, service_life_choices=[1.0,0.5,0.75], explicit_event_share=0.0, change_list_share=0.0): B3-01.by_year[1] reference 0.0, unified 2.8990143619012088e-12, error 2.21e-9. Frequency: 63 of 6900 random option-fuzz scenarios (all with an included-stage subset or a short period); 754 of 2016 in a targeted family (stage subsets containing B3, two or more lives sharing event years); 114 of 5040 all-stage scenarios with T <= 10 and lives <= 4 years (max 2.2e-9). B3-01.value and all summary-mode leaves are unaffected. On the study's own population distribution with fresh seeds (600 scenarios) there were 0 differences. Which side departs: the unified model; B3-01's definition says a year containing the row's renewal carries no repair. Scripts: t5_b3_residue.py, t5b_allstages.py, repro.py section F1.
findings.proposed_fix: Build the yearly repair series additively: per cycle group, add rsum*w[y] only to the years not in that group's event-year set (plus one group for rows without renewals), instead of subtracting from a grand total; or clamp/zero years in which all contributing groups are skipped. Add stage-subset cases containing B3 with short lives to population.edge_cases, and report the claim with the detail-mode series stated separately.

findings.area: Defective input: factor reference without a factor record (non-numeric leaves)
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/engine.py lines 351, 688, 898-914; unit SYS-03 (violations), both detail modes
findings.claim_refuted: Exact reproduction of every leaf on defective scenarios. SYS-03.violations differs whenever a referenced factor id is absent from scn.factors, and for None in several mandatory slots. The study's eight defect kinds contain no missing-factor defect, so verify_unified.py never exercised it.
findings.evidence: Repro 1: scn = synth.make_scenario(16,'RC','office','S',60.0, n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=4); scn.equipment[0].factor_id = scn.equipment[1].factor_id = 'F-NOT-IN-TABLE'. Reference violations ['equipment[0].factor_id (no factor)', 'equipment[1].factor_id (no factor)'], unified ['F-NOT-IN-TABLE (no factor)'] (n_checked 181 and n_references_affected 2 agree). Repro 2 (composite_share=1.0, epd_share=0.0): routes[0].factor_id = None on materials[0], water_waste.waste_factor_id = None, materials[1].composition[0].factor_id = None, summary_quantities.concrete_uptake_factor_id = 'F-NOT-IN-TABLE'. Reference: ['materials[0].end_of_life.routes[0].factor_id (no factor)', 'materials[1].composition[0].factor_id (no factor)', 'summary_quantities.concrete_uptake_factor_id (no factor)', 'water_waste.waste_factor_id (no factor)']; unified: ['None (no factor)', 'factors{F-NOT-IN-TABLE}.licence_status', 'materials[0].end_of_life.routes (no factor)', 'water_waste.municipal_waste_factor_id (no factor)']. In the single-mutation fuzz every 'dangling factor id' mutation differed (6/6 runs for each of 12 slots), as did route factor None (6/6), all operation factor ids None (6/6) and deleting a factor record (5/6). Which side departs: mixed. For unknown ids the SYS-03 docstring says unusable factors are reported per factor id, which the unified model does and the reference code does not (it reports per reference path), so the definition and the reference disagree. For None ids the unified model departs: it prints 'None', drops the route index, names an attribute that does not exist (municipal_waste_factor_id; the model field is waste_factor_id) and reports a licence problem for a record that is absent. Script: repro.py section F2.
findings.proposed_fix: Decide the label rule in the SYS-03 docstring (per path or per id for absent records) and make both sides follow it; in engine.py build the none_refs paths from the same strings as model.factor_references (routes[j].factor_id, water_waste.waste_factor_id, composition[j].factor_id, epd.factor_id, summary_quantities.concrete_uptake_factor_id). Add a MISSING_FACTOR defect kind to synth/generate.py and to the verification population.

findings.area: Baseline comparison: crash on cyclic baselines
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/engine.py line 893 (evaluate(base_scn, detail=False) evaluates the baseline's own SUM-08); unit SUM-08
findings.claim_refuted: "A crash in either implementation on an input the other handles": the unified model raises RecursionError where the reference returns a result, in both detail modes.
findings.evidence: Repro: scn = synth.make_scenario(11,'RC','office','S',60.0, n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=4); population.BASELINES[scn.meta.scenario_id] = scn; scn.boundary.baseline_scenario = scn.meta.scenario_id. Reference SUM-08 = {'status': 'COMPARED', 'baseline': 6998738.960941015, 'delta': 0.0, 'saving': 0.0}; engine.evaluate(scn, detail=True) and detail=False both raise RecursionError. Same with two comparable scenarios naming each other as baseline (reference delta -270.00721996463835, unified RecursionError). A non-cyclic chain P -> B -> C gives no difference. Which side departs: the unified model; SUM-08's definition computes the baseline's whole-life total only, the unified model recursively evaluates the baseline's own comparison. Script: t3_targeted.py sections 1, 2, 2b; repro.py F5.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the baseline total without its SUM-08 (a flag that skips the comparison step, or a guard set of ids in progress), and add self-baseline and mutual-baseline cases to the edge cases.

findings.area: Baseline comparison: result depends on hidden cache state
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/engine.py lines 43-47 and 890-893 (_BASELINE_TOTALS keyed by base_scn.meta.scenario_id, never invalidated); unit SUM-08; bench/verify_unified.py lines 60-63
findings.claim_refuted: evaluate(scn) reproduces SUM-08. That holds only if clear_baseline_cache() is called first, which verify_unified.py does before every call in the exactness test; the cached path that the load benchmark times is never checked for correctness against a changed baseline.
findings.evidence: Repro: p = synth.make_scenario(14,'RC','office','S',60.0, scenario_id='STALE-P', n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=4); base = population.attach_baseline(p); engine.clear_baseline_cache(); engine.evaluate(p, detail=False); then double every non-missing base.materials[i].quantity; evaluate again without clearing. Reference SUM-08: baseline 9435248.657708215, delta -1508640.6488980716, saving 0.15989410598793. Unified without clear: baseline 8390173.315520307, delta -463565.3067101566, saving 0.05525098103189888. After clear it agrees. Second case: a new proposal generated with the same scenario_id and attach_baseline called again (registers the same '<id>-BASELINE' key): reference delta -475586.16128587537, saving +0.0454; unified delta +569489.1809020303, saving -0.0604 (sign reversed). Which side departs: the unified model; the SUM-08 definition says the baseline is computed from scratch. Script: t3_targeted.py sections 3 and 3b; repro.py F6.
findings.proposed_fix: Key the cache on the baseline object's content (or identity plus a version stamp), or drop the module-level cache and let the caller pass a precomputed baseline total explicitly. In verify_unified.py add a check that evaluates with a warm cache after the baseline has changed, and say in the load report that the cached timing assumes an unchanged baseline.

findings.area: Closed form: refrigerant leak loses precision at small leak rates
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/closed_forms.py refrigerant_device lines 147-152 (leaked += m - after, with after = m*(1-rate)**whole); units B1-02 (value, by_item), X-02/B1
findings.claim_refuted: "each function in closed_forms.py equals the loop it replaces" (docstring: same number up to rounding of a different operation order). The subtraction cancels, so the relative error of the leaked mass is about 1.2e-16/rate, which passes 1e-9 for rates below roughly 1e-7.
findings.evidence: Direct comparison with my own yearly loop, T=60, m0=100, no top-up, no events: rate 1e-7: loop 0.000599998230003422, closed form 0.0005999982296884809 (5.2e-10); rate 1e-8: 5.999998230000343e-05 vs 5.999998261074779e-05 (5.2e-9); rate 1e-9: 2.7e-8; rate 1e-12: 2.2e-5. Random fuzz (170000 iterations): worst relative difference 1.6e-9 at rate 1e-7, 1.3e-7 at 1e-9, 1.2e-4 at 1e-12; at rates >= 1e-3 the worst was 1.1e-13; 'before' and 'end' masses always agreed to 1.2e-12. Scenario level: mutation 'annual_leak_rate = 1e-9 on all devices', all stages (T=59.999999): B1-02.value reference 0.0018266189670990837, unified 0.0018266189279354532, error 1.04e-8 by the study's measure; with leak rate 1e-8 and included stages ['B1'] (seed 31): 0.0014912033580525403 vs 0.0014912033658532663, error 5.2e-9. Realistic leak rates (percent per year) are unaffected. Which side departs: the unified model's closed form. Scripts: t4_closed_forms.py, repro.py F7.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute the cycle leak without cancellation, e.g. leaked += -m*math.expm1(whole*math.log1p(-rate)) for 0 < rate < 1, or fall back to the yearly loop when rate < 1e-6. Extend tests/test_closed_forms.py to rates down to 1e-12 with a relative tolerance on the leaked mass itself.

findings.area: Closed form: grid_cumulative outside well-formed descriptors
findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/closed_forms.py grid_cumulative lines 100-124; units X-11, B6-03, B2-01 (when demand profiles are CONSTANT), X-06
findings.claim_refuted: grid_cumulative equals the X-06 loop. It does for CONSTANT, for LINEAR_DECLINE_TO_FLOOR with decline >= 0 or start >= floor, and for STEPWISE lists sorted by from_index starting at 0 (worst relative difference 4.3e-16 over 170000 iterations). It does not for three malformed descriptors.
findings.evidence: (a) Unsorted steps: steps [(from_index 10, 0.2), (0, 0.5)], T=20: X-06 loop (last step in list order with from_index <= k) sums to 10.0, grid_cumulative returns 7.0 (it sorts first). Scenario level, grid.steps reversed: X-11.value reference 30249787.528304957, unified 9186901.603083286. (b) First step from_index > 0 (scn.operation.grid.steps[0].from_index = 2 on synth.make_scenario(41,'RC','office','S',60.0, grid_kind='STEPWISE', profile_kind='CONSTANT', n_materials=12, n_equipment=6, n_refrigerants=4)): reference raises TypeError at refcalc/units_b.py:371, unified detail raises TypeError at engine.py:1075, unified summary returns a result (uncovered years count as factor 0). (c) LINEAR_DECLINE_TO_FLOOR with start=0.3, annual_decline=-0.01, floor=0.5, T=30: loop 15.450000000000001, grid_cumulative 13.349999999999998 (the d <= 0 branch ignores the floor). Which side departs: (c) the closed form; (a) and (b) the definition is ambiguous (the X-06 docstring says 'the value of the applicable step'; the model docstring says 'last step with from_index <= k' without saying last in list order or by index) and the reference crashes on (b). Scripts: t4_closed_forms.py, repro.py F8/F9.
findings.proposed_fix: In grid_cumulative handle d <= 0 with start < floor (return the loop, or compute the crossing index for a rising line); do not sort steps (or validate sortedness and first from_index == 0 and fall back to the loop otherwise). State the STEPWISE rule precisely in the X-06 docstring and add a reference check for malformed step lists.

findings.unit_or_file: fastcalc/closed_forms.py lines 35 and 150; fastcalc/engine.py summary path; refcalc/units_c_sum.py line 349
findings.claim_refuted: "A crash in either implementation on an input the other handles" for inputs outside the generator's range.
findings.evidence: (1) materials[0].refresh_cycle = float('nan') (seed 15, T=60): reference returns a result (no events), unified raises ValueError 'cannot convert float NaN to integer' in renewal_count (int(T/period)); float('inf') gives no difference. (2) refrigerants[0].annual_leak_rate = 1e12 with top_up False and no change events: reference returns B1-02 = nan, unified raises OverflowError at closed_forms.py:150 ((1-rate)**whole). (3) study_period = -5.0: reference IndexError (units_c_sum.py:349), unified detail IndexError (engine.py:1092), unified summary returns SUM-03 = 1107393.5415871232; study_period = 0 and 0.0 give no difference. (4) study_period = 200 with 130-entry tables and CONSTANT profiles/grid: reference and unified detail raise IndexError, unified summary returns a result. None of these inputs is valid; the generator refuses or never produces them. Scripts: t3_targeted.py, t6_more.py, repro.py F10.
findings.proposed_fix: Either validate the inputs up front on both sides (T > 0, finite positive cycles, 0 <= rate <= 1, table length >= ceil(T)) and return a uniform error, or guard renewal_count against non-finite periods. Document that results for such inputs are undefined.

checks_performed:
All scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user--/49c0bd7e-a786-5ae4-9a1e-e89e7996ede3/scratchpad/verify/lens1/ (h.py harness, muts.py mutation catalogue, t1..t7, repro.py). Every scenario was compared for all 69 units with common.compare.compare(ref, cand, floor=1e-9*|SUM-03|), in detail=True (including extra leaves) and detail=False (ignore_missing=True), with the baseline cache cleared before each call; exceptions on either side were recorded. The repository was not modified (git status clean, python -B).

Scenario comparisons: about 32,700 in total.
1. Option fuzz, no mutation (t1_options.py, seeds 777001, 20250001, 987654321): 6,900 scenarios. Random seeds, all structures and uses, S with n_materials/n_equipment/n_refrigerants in {0,1,2,...} and about 3 % M; study periods 0.01 to 300 including values just below/above integers (1e-12, 1e-9, 2^-40 offsets); every make_scenario option in random combination (profile and grid kinds, life modes, explicit service_life_choices with sub-year lives, exact divisors, near-divisors and nextafter(T), top_up, composite/EPD shares, unit_variety, event-list shares, replacement cycle and reconstruction scenario, CO2_ONLY, random included-stage subsets including empty, table_length); 45 % dirty with single defect kinds, combinations, defect_share up to 1.0; baselines comparable and not comparable (area, period, stages, scope, factor version, zero baseline, missing id). Result: 63 differences, all the B3-01/X-07 yearly-series residue.
2. Single-mutation fuzz (t2_mutations.py single): 644 mutations, each applied alone to 5-6 base scenarios, 7,024 scenarios. Mutations cover None / 0 / int 0 / negative / 1e-12 / 1e12 / boundary values in every numeric field the calculations read, cycles and lives (T, T/2, T/3, T/7, sub-year, nextafter(T), ints), explicit event lists (empty, [T], [0], negative, duplicates, unsorted, non-integer, same year, last partial year, mixed int/float), leak rates 0, 1, 1e-4 to 1e-12, 1.5, top_up True/False/None/int, factor ids None and unknown in every slot, unlicensed/empty-source/changed-stage/changed-unit factors, deleted factor records, unit strings without conversion, row conversion overrides and conflicting table entries, composition variants (empty, boundary fraction sums, same specification with different content, repeated or unusable components, EPD on composites), route variants, states and provenance, gwp and gas list changes, construction, operation, water, end-of-life, project, boundary and summary-quantity fields, profile and grid descriptor changes, baselines.
3. Combined mutations (2-4 at once): 3,999 unrestricted and 6,000 with the already-identified triggers excluded. The restricted run gave 4 differences, all rounding/cancellation with 1e12-scale values.
4. Targeted families: 2,016 + 5,040 valid scenarios for the B3 yearly series; 720 dirty scenarios with each defect kind alone and all together (share 0.02 and 1.0, 10 periods): 0 differences; 420 exact-multiple and near-multiple cycle scenarios (T from 1 to 300, lives T/k, replacement cycles T/k): 0 differences; the study's own verification_population with fresh seeds 424242 and 31415926 (600 scenarios, S and M): 0 differences.
5. Targeted probes: self/mutual/chained baselines, stale cache, near-identical baseline (no difference), NaN/inf cycles, study_period 0, 0.0, negative, int, beyond table length, events around the last partial year (no difference).

Closed forms (t4_closed_forms.py, 170,000 iterations against loops I wrote from the conventions in refcalc/base.py): renewal_count identical to counting in every case, including T = k*L, L = nextafter(T/k), L below 1; skip_weight_periodic worst difference 0; skip_weight_events 5.6e-17; linear_weighted_sum 4.4e-16; grid_cumulative CONSTANT / valid LINEAR / sorted STEPWISE at most 4.3e-16; refrigerant_device before/end masses at most 1.2e-12, leaked mass at most 1.1e-13 for rates >= 1e-3. Failures are the ones reported (small leak rates, malformed grid descriptors).

No difference was found for: non-permitted licences, units without conversion, CO2_ONLY scope, comparable and non-comparable baselines (with the cache cleared), composite rows sharing a specification label, duplicated/unsorted/non-integer event years, change years equal to T, leak rates 0 and 1, top_up either way, n_* of 0 and 1, sub-year cycles, or any of the study's eight defect kinds.
could_not_check: Size L scenarios (20,000 material rows) were not run; size M made up roughly 3 % of the option fuzz plus about a third of the 600 study-population scenarios. Cycles shorter than about T/4000 were avoided because the reference enumerates every event; NaN or infinite study periods and wrong-type inputs (strings, non-integer GridStep.from_index) were not tested. I did not check the reference functions against their docstrings except where a difference led there, did not read tests/test_closed_forms.py, did not regenerate 04_VERIFICATION/unified_model_exactness.json, and did not examine the timing or memory claims. The effect of the stale baseline cache on the published load figures was not measured.
overall:
The claim is refuted as stated, but it holds on the population the study actually tested. On the study's own distribution with fresh seeds (600 scenarios), on each of its eight defect kinds alone (720) and on exact cycle multiples (420) I found zero differences, and the time-handling closed forms (renewal count, skipped-year weights, linear sums, well-formed grid sums) matched my own loops to 5e-16 over 170,000 trials.

Where it fails:
- Valid scenarios: the detail-mode yearly repair series (B3-01.by_year, carried into X-07) is built by subtraction and leaves residues, sometimes negative, where the reference is exactly zero. This exceeds the study's 1e-9 criterion in 63 of 6,900 random valid/dirty scenarios (up to 1.6e-4 with included stages ['B3']; up to 2.2e-9 with all stages and short periods). Absolute sizes are around 1e-10 kgCO2e; totals and summary mode are unaffected.
- Defective scenarios outside the study's eight defect kinds: when a grid table or an annual profile table disagrees with its descriptor, whole-life totals differ materially (0.6 % and 0.007 % in the minimal cases, unbounded in general) and the unified model's own outputs contradict each other. A factor reference without a factor record gives different SYS-03 violation labels.
- Baselines: a scenario that is its own baseline (or two that name each other) makes the unified model raise RecursionError; the baseline total is cached by scenario id only, so editing or re-registering a baseline returns a stale delta (sign reversed in one reproduction) unless the cache is cleared, which the study's exactness test always does.
- Closed forms: refrigerant_device loses precision for leak rates below about 1e-7; grid_cumulative is wrong for unsorted or gapped step lists and for a negative decline with start below floor.

Every finding has a minimal construction and both values in repro.py.
